leg: LANE A — Halloween Experience Reality Check, Oct 30 – Nov 1 2026 (family of 5: adults + 16/13/8), must end in Dublin for EI61
summary: You did NOT wrongly write off Dublin — but you wrote off the wrong thing. Bram Stoker IS Oct 23–26 (officially confirmed; aggregator sites claiming Oct 30–Nov 2 are extrapolating from 2025 and are wrong). Dublin CITY has no Halloween parade on Oct 31 — that is a documented hoax trap, not an oversight. BUT 70 miles up the road, DERRY HALLOWEEN runs Oct 28–31 2026 — Europe's largest Halloween festival, its 40TH ANNIVERSARY, 100,000+ attendees, and its two headline events land exactly on your target nights: the Awakening the Walled City "City of Bones" trail on Oct 30 (£1/person) and the Carnival Parade (7pm) + fireworks over the River Foyle (8:15pm) on Oct 31 — both FREE. That is the answer. The remarkable part: the CHEAPEST flight you have (DBV–DUB Oct 25, $813) is also the one that unlocks the best itinerary — it lands you for the final two days of Bram Stoker (Oct 25–26), leaves four days in Dublin, then a ~€20pp coach to Derry for Oct 29–Nov 1, back for EI61. Best experience and cheapest airfare are the SAME choice, which almost never happens. Ranking by experience: 1) Derry 9/10, 2) Lucca 7/10 (10 for the 16yo, 3–4 for the 8yo in Sat/Sun crushes), 3) Púca 6/10, 4) Edinburgh Samhuinn 6/10, 5) Dublin city alone 5/10, 6) Vienna Prater Halloween 4/10. IF YOU ONLY CARE ABOUT THE MEMORY: DERRY. IF COST MATTERS EQUALLY: ALSO DERRY — its headline events are free and the routing flight is your cheapest. The one thing that can kill it is Derry lodging for 5 on Oct 30–31, which books out months ahead and must be secured NOW.
caveats: CONFIDENCE LABELS, honestly: (1) CONFIRMED — Bram Stoker Oct 23–26 2026 (bramstokerfestival.com + official socials); Derry Halloween Oct 28–31 2026 40th anniversary (derryhalloween.com, visitderry.com, Derry City & Strabane Council); Púca Oct 29–Nov 1 and its 16+/18+ age gates (pucafestival.com essential-info); Lucca Oct 28–Nov 1 60th and Sept 1 ticket resale date (luccacomicsandgames.com/TicketOne); Nov 1 2026 is NOT an Irish public holiday (it IS one in Austria and Italy). (2) 2025-CARRIED-OVER, not yet republished for 2026 — Derry's exact times (trail 6–9pm Oct 28–30; parade 7pm; fireworks 8:15pm Oct 31) come from the site's own FAQ which still shows 2025; the 2026 programme drops late Sept/Oct. Structure has been stable for years, but VERIFY before booking non-refundable lodging. The £1/person trail ticket is a NEW 2026 pilot approved at June council committee (Bishop St Car Park + Upper Walls only) — booking mechanism not yet published. (3) ESTIMATED, NOT QUOTED — I did not obtain live lodging quotes for Derry or live 5-seat fares for PSA–DUB or VIE–DUB. Derry lodging figures are historical-typical and are the single biggest risk in this plan. (4) HARD WARNINGS: Do NOT trust any third-party site listing a Dublin city Halloween parade — in 2024 an AI-generated listing put thousands on O'Connell Street for an event that did not exist and Gardaí had to disperse them. Several "Dublin Halloween 2026" pages I hit repeat the wrong Bram Stoker dates and a phantom Macnas parade; they are the same category of content. (5) There is NO late-night public transport from Derry back to Dublin on Oct 31 — the ~21:38 train only reaches Belfast and the 22:00 coach goes to Belfast. If you watch the fireworks you sleep in Derry (or Letterkenny/Limavady/Strabane/Coleraine). Non-negotiable. (6) Derry is in the UK — Common Travel Area means no passport control at the land border, but currency is GBP and phone roaming may switch. (7) Lucca: tickets are in a DEAD WINDOW right now — Early Bird closed Jul 27, regular sale opens Sept 1 2026. You cannot buy today. Lucca historic centre is 99% occupied for Oct 31–Nov 1 with ~8 properties left for TWO people from €492; a party of 5 in Lucca centre on Halloween is effectively unavailable. (8) The 5-seat constraint that has shaped this whole trip applies again to any Lucca or Vienna exit — PSA–DUB and VIE–DUB both need a 5-seat check, and Ryanair's WINTER schedule starts late Oct 2026 and may thin PSA–DUB. (9) The 8-year-old is the binding constraint on Lucca (100k people in medieval streets, guidance is "use a carrier not a stroller") and on Edinburgh Samhuinn (organiser warns of semi-nudity and uninhibited behaviour, parental discretion advised; 3 hours outdoors on Calton Hill at night in late October).

options.label: RANK 1 — DERRY HALLOWEEN, Oct 28–31 2026 (40th anniversary). THE ANSWER.
options.detail: Europe's largest Halloween festival, 100,000+ attendees, voted Best Halloween Destination by USA TODAY readers, celebrating 40 YEARS in 2026 with theme 'The Awakening' / 'City of Bones'. Your two target nights are its two best: OCT 30 = final night of the Awakening the Walled City Trail, 6–9pm, an illuminated after-dark route through Guildhall Square, Shipquay St, the Diamond, Bishop St, Cathedral Quarter and the 400-year-old walls, using pyrotechnics, aerial performance, projection and music. OCT 31 = Carnival Parade at 7pm (grassroots community procession, ~40,000 spectators, costumes encouraged) followed by the fireworks finale over the River Foyle at ~8:15pm. Both parade and fireworks are FREE and unticketed. Also running: 'Little Horrors' children's strand (crafts, costume dress-up, kids' shows, storytelling), 'Freaky Family Fun', the 'Heart of Samhain' hub at Guildhall Square with live music and street food, Samhain baking demos, plus named 2026 shows 'Witchy Wonderland: A Disco of the Undead' on the upper walls, 'It's In Our Bones' aerial spectacle at The Diamond, and 'Walters Wake: A Jazz Funeral'. NEW for 2026: a £1-per-person pilot ticket for the trail (approved June 2026) purely to manage crowding at Bishop Street Car Park and the Upper Walls — £5 for your party.
options.source: https://derryhalloween.com/ + https://www.visitderry.com/whats-on/derry-halloween + https://www.derrystrabane.com/what-s-on/events-(sv)/derry-halloween-2026/1017971 + https://www.derryjournal.com/news/politics/council/ps1-tickets-for-awakening-the-walled-city-at-derry-halloween-to-be-introduced-8741400
options.experience_score: 9/10 — the only option where all three ages get a top-tier experience at the SAME time: Little Horrors and the costume-street atmosphere for the 8yo, the City of Bones trail and pyrotechnics for the 13yo, and genuine 100k-person festival scale plus a fireworks finale over a river for the 16yo. Contained in a walkable walled city rather than a crush, and the headline acts cost nothing.
options.dates: Oct 28–31 2026; you want Oct 30 (trail) + Oct 31 (parade 7pm, fireworks 8:15pm)
options.notes: Times are carried from the site's own 2025 FAQ — the 2026 programme publishes late Sept/Oct. Structure has been stable for years. Nov 1: festival is OVER and Derry is quiet — that is your travel day back toward Dublin, which suits EI61 on Nov 2 perfectly.

options.label: THE CONVERGENCE — your CHEAPEST flight is also the one that unlocks the best trip
options.detail: DBV–DUB Oct 25 at $813 for 5 is not just the cheapest of your three Dublin options ($1,650 Oct 30 / $1,158 Nov 1) — it is the one that makes the whole plan work. Landing Oct 25 puts you in Dublin for the FINAL TWO DAYS of Bram Stoker (Oct 25–26, incl. the Oct 26 bank holiday Monday), which you had assumed was lost. Then Oct 27–28 in Dublin (museums, Emerald Park, Malahide), coach to Derry Oct 29 or 30, Derry Oct 30–31 for the trail + parade + fireworks, coach back Nov 1, EI61 Nov 2. You capture Ireland's flagship gothic festival AND Europe's largest Halloween festival on one $813 flight. Choosing Oct 30 instead costs $837 MORE and forfeits Bram Stoker entirely and half of Derry.
options.source: User-verified live Ryanair fare + https://www.bramstokerfestival.com/ + https://www.aircoach.ie/derry-londonderry
options.experience_score: 10/10 on routing efficiency — best experience and lowest airfare are the same decision, which is rare enough to act on immediately.
options.dates: Fly DBV–DUB Oct 25; Derry Oct 29/30–Nov 1; EI61 Nov 2
options.notes: Also sidesteps the Oct 27/28 DBV–DUB seat problem (only 3 and 2 seats) entirely. Trade-off to be honest about: you swap ~5 nights of cheap Dubrovnik lodging ($78–120) for Dublin nights ($166–482) — roughly $400–1,500 of extra lodging. That is the real price of the Oct 25 departure, and it is what buys you Bram Stoker plus a relaxed run-up to Derry.

options.label: Derry logistics — the ONLY hard part, and it needs booking now
options.detail: GETTING THERE without a car is easy and cheap: Aircoach 705X runs Dublin City Centre + Dublin Airport to Derry (Foyleside), direct, ~22 services daily, from £19/€20pp, ~4–4.5h routed via Belfast; 10% family discount booking online; contactless only, no cash on this route. Alternative: Translink X4 Dublin Busáras–Derry, roughly every 2 hours, ~5h30. Round trip for 5 ≈ €200–250. GETTING BACK is the constraint: there is NO late option to Dublin on Oct 31 — the extra 21:38 train only reaches Belfast, the 22:38 only reaches Coleraine, and the 22:00 212 bus goes to Belfast. If you watch the fireworks, you sleep in Derry. LODGING is the real risk: Derry fills months ahead for Halloween and Oct 31 (a Saturday in 2026) is the peak night of the peak year (40th anniversary). Fallbacks within reach: Letterkenny (Co. Donegal, Republic), Limavady, Strabane, Coleraine — all short bus/taxi hops.
options.source: https://www.aircoach.ie/derry-londonderry + https://www.translink.co.uk/special-events/derry-halloween + https://www.derrystrabane.com/news/additional-translink-services-for-derry-halloween-announced
options.experience_score: n/a — logistics. But note a Translink Family & Friends ticket (2 adults + 4 children, unlimited travel, ~£23) covers local movement once you are in Northern Ireland.
options.dates: Coach Dublin→Derry Oct 29 or 30; 3 nights Derry (Oct 29/30/31); coach back Nov 1
options.notes: Estimate = ~$250 coach for 5 round trip + ~$1,000 for 3 nights of family accommodation for 5. I did NOT get live quotes — this is the number most likely to move, and it can move a lot upward on Oct 31. ACTION: book Derry lodging before anything else in this plan; everything else here is flexible and this is not.

options.label: RANK 2 — LUCCA COMICS & GAMES 60th, Oct 28–Nov 1. Highest ceiling, worst fit for the 8-year-old.
options.detail: Genuinely world-class and a real once-only: the 60th anniversary ('LUCCA60: Legacy'), under European Commission patronage, poster by Claudio Castellini. Last edition sold 280,000+ tickets with 750,000+ total attendances, 900 international guests, 730 exhibitors. TICKETS: you are in a dead window — Early Bird ran Jun 23–Jul 27 2026 and is CLOSED; regular box office opens SEPT 1 2026 at list price, roughly €22–30/day. Named ticket + wristband required. For your party: the 8yo is likely FREE (2025 rule was children born after 1 Jan 2016 free with a ticketed adult — verify the 2026 cutoff), so 4 paying × ~€28 × 2 days ≈ €225. Kids' provision is real — 'Lucca Junior' has free workshops, puppet shows and interactive games, and Family Palace, Self Area, Area Pro, IMT Library and Giardino degli Osservanti are free-access. CROWD REALITY, unvarnished: ~100,000 people compressed into a small walled medieval city on peak days, streets packed wall-to-wall. Official-adjacent guidance is to use a CARRIER rather than a stroller and to escape onto the city walls for breathing room. Wed 29 / Thu 30 are the sane days with children — which is precisely the wrong end of your window, since Oct 31 (Sat) and Nov 1 (Sun holiday) are the peak of the peak.
options.source: https://lucca2026.luccacomicsandgames.com/it/biglietti + https://www.ticketone.it/artist/lucca-comics-games/giornaliero-lucca-comics-games-2026-4181099/ + https://fumettologica.it/2026/06/biglietti-lucca-comics-2026-early-bird/
options.experience_score: 7/10 as a family average, but that number hides the variance: 10/10 for the 16-year-old (probably a lifetime memory), 7/10 for the 13, and 3–4/10 for the 8-year-old on Oct 31–Nov 1, who will spend the day at waist height in a 100,000-person crush. If your 16-year-old is deep into comics/gaming/cosplay this is the one option that beats Derry FOR HIM specifically — it does not beat Derry for the household.
options.dates: Oct 28–Nov 1 2026 (tickets on sale Sept 1 2026)
options.notes: Free-access Palazzo Guinigi exhibitions need no ticket. 'Skip the Welcome Desk' costs €9.99 extra for daily/2-day tickets and must be bought by 09:00 Oct 16.

options.label: Lucca — the lodging and exit problem that probably disqualifies it
options.detail: LUCCA CENTRE IS GONE: as of late July 2026 Italian press reported the historic centre at 99% occupancy for the night of Oct 31–Nov 1, with about EIGHT properties left for TWO people starting at €492, and platform rates approaching €2,000 for a single weekend night. A party of five in Lucca centre on Halloween is effectively unavailable. Best remaining stock: PISA (77% occupancy, ~120 properties, €86–798) — widest availability and softest ceiling, ~30 min by train. VIAREGGIO (89%, 57 properties, €100–1,323) — 20 min by train, and several hotels bundle the event ticket or train ticket into the stay. MONTECATINI TERME (72%, 46 properties, €87–1,338). Florence is a ~1h20 commute usually with a change — fallback only. DO NOT DRIVE: the road network around Lucca is completely restructured under an extraordinary access plan during the event and the Lucca Est exit congests fast; train is strongly preferable and Lucca station sits right outside the walls. THE EXIT: Pisa–Dublin is direct on Ryanair (FR5020, ~15:00 daily) and Aer Lingus, ~12 flights/week, ~2h45–3h. But Ryanair's WINTER schedule starts late Oct 2026 and may thin the route, and you need FIVE seats on one aircraft on Nov 1 (the festival's last day and peak exodus) or Nov 2 against EI61.
options.source: https://www.iltirreno.it/lucca/cronaca/2026/07/25/news/lucca-comics-2026-allarme-alloggi-una-notte-puo-costare-quasi-2-000-euro-1.100899302 + https://www.flightsfrom.com/PSA-DUB
options.experience_score: n/a — logistics. This is the leg where the Lucca option most plausibly breaks: 5-seat availability on PSA–DUB in the winter-schedule changeover, on the single busiest departure day of the Tuscan year, with no slack before EI61.
options.dates: 3 nights Pisa Oct 29–Nov 1; PSA–DUB Nov 1 or Nov 2
options.notes: Estimate = ~3 nights Pisa family accommodation (~€250/night) + local Pisa↔Lucca trains (~€80) + PSA–DUB for 5 ($400–900, unverified). Compared to Derry this is more expensive, more fragile, and worse for your youngest. It is the right answer ONLY if the 16-year-old's specific passion outweighs everything else.

options.label: RANK 3 — PÚCA FESTIVAL, Oct 29–Nov 1, Trim + Athboy, Co. Meath. Authentic, free — and thinner than its marketing.
options.detail: Be skeptical, and here is the specific reason: the ticketed spine of this festival is AGE-GATED AWAY FROM YOUR FAMILY. Big Top events are STRICTLY 16+ and Samhain Circus is STRICTLY 18+. That means the entire headline programme — Glen Hansard, The Coronas with Róisín O, Hothouse Flowers, Enya Martin, John Colleary, the Bluebird Absurd burlesque shows — is off-limits to your 13- and 8-year-olds. Only your 16-year-old qualifies, and only if already 16. What remains, and it IS genuinely good and FREE: the PÚCA PROCESSION in Trim (Oct 30, free, non-ticketed — giant spirits, drumming, fire performance through medieval streets, billed as the Gathering of the Spirits), the LIGHTING OF THE SAMHAIN FIRE at Athboy Fair Green on Oct 31 (free, ceremonially linking Tlachtga, Tara, Loughcrew, Tailteann and Uisneach), free projections on Trim Castle, the Harvest Market from 11am daily, and 'Sorcas na Samhna' — the all-ages family Celtic circus in Athboy's big tent (distinct from the 18+ Samhain Circus). ON THE 'BIRTHPLACE OF HALLOWEEN' CLAIM: it is legitimate, not invented. Tlachtga / the Hill of Ward at Athboy is a genuine archaeological site associated with the Samhain fire ritual, and the festival is a Fáilte Ireland / Meath County Council production, not a private promoter. But the honest on-the-ground product for a family is a free street procession, a free bonfire ceremony, a market and a circus tent, across two small towns 20–30 min apart — call it 4–6 hours of real content over two evenings.
options.source: https://pucafestival.com/essential-info/ + https://pucafestival.com/all-days/ + https://pucafestival.com/event/the-samhain-fire/ + https://pucafestival.com/travel/
options.experience_score: 6/10 — the most AUTHENTIC Samhain on this list and almost entirely free, but thin for a full weekend, and its marquee ticketed content excludes two of your three kids. Excellent as a Dublin-based day/overnight SUPPLEMENT; weak as the centrepiece of your Halloween.
options.dates: Oct 29–Nov 1 2026. Procession Trim Oct 30; Samhain Fire Athboy Oct 31
options.notes: CAR-FREE ACCESS IS SOLVED: an official festival coach runs from Dublin Busáras (~50–60 min), historically departing ~14:00 and returning from Athboy ~23:00 / Trim ~23:30, booked separately from event tickets, on sale around LATE AUGUST — i.e. imminent. A free shuttle runs hourly between Trim and Athboy all four days. Bus Éireann also serves both towns with extra festival services; alternatively Dublin Connolly→Enfield by rail (~every 30 min) then a local link. Bag limit 40x40x20cm.

options.label: RANK 4 — EDINBURGH SAMHUINN FIRE FESTIVAL, Oct 31, Calton Hill. Spectacular, but read the content warning.
options.detail: The creative wildcard that genuinely competes on spectacle. Run by Beltane Fire Society (a community arts charity since 1988; Samhuinn since 1995, on Calton Hill since 2018), it stages the overthrow of Summer by Winter as a battle between the Summer and Winter Kings — fire-dancing, acrobatics, massed drumming, 20+ stage performances and a large bonfire, roughly 7–10pm on Oct 31. THE HONEST CAVEATS, which are the organiser's own words: the event contains SEMI-NUDITY AND UNINHIBITED BEHAVIOUR, parental discretion advised, and under-16s must be accompanied by a full-paying adult. Add three hours standing outdoors on an exposed hill in Edinburgh in late October. TICKETS: 2026 tickets are NOT yet on sale; sold ONLY via Citizen Ticket (the society warns any other platform is selling non-genuine tickets), announced first on beltane.org and their Facebook. It sold out in 2025 with a waiting list. Edinburgh→Dublin is trivially easy for the return (Ryanair and Aer Lingus, many daily) — logistically this is the SECOND-easiest option after Derry.
options.source: https://beltane.org/about-samhuinn/ + https://edinburgh.org/event/samhuinn-fire-festival/
options.experience_score: 6/10 — arguably a 9 for your 16-year-old and a 2 for your 8-year-old. The content warning plus a cold, late, standing, adult-toned pagan fire ritual makes this the wrong call with an 8-year-old in the party. If this were a trip for two adults and the 16-year-old, it would rank second overall.
options.dates: Sat Oct 31 2026, ~7–10pm, Calton Hill (2026 ticket sale date not yet announced)
options.notes: Price is an estimate for 5 based on prior-year tiers; 2026 pricing unpublished. Watch beltane.org — it sells out. Also note this competes head-on with Derry for the exact same evening and Derry costs nothing.

options.label: RANK 5 — DUBLIN CITY, Oct 30 – Nov 1. Correcting your write-off: not dead, but not a destination.
options.detail: CONFIRMING YOUR PREMISE: Bram Stoker Festival 2026 IS Fri Oct 23 – Mon Oct 26 ('Four Days & Nights of Deadly Adventures'), officially, matching the Irish October bank holiday Monday of Oct 26. Multiple travel sites list Oct 30–Nov 2; they are WRONG, extrapolating from 2025's Oct 31–Nov 3. So Dublin's flagship is over before your window. AND THERE IS NO DUBLIN HALLOWEEN PARADE — this is a documented trap: on Oct 31 2024 an AI-generated listing on a US site advertised a 'Macnas Halloween Parade' from Parnell St to Christ Church; thousands turned up, Gardaí had to disperse them, and the Luas was disrupted. Trust only bramstokerfestival.com, dublincity.ie and Macnas's own channels. WHAT IS ACTUALLY REAL on your nights: Dublin City Council runs a genuine, mostly FREE, neighbourhood-scale Halloween programme running through Oct 31 — the strongest being OTHERWORLD FESTIVAL in Ballymun on Oct 31 (a long-running community festival: parade, then ~3 hours of entertainment 6–9pm with funfair rides, Circus Gerbola, a main stage, monster play zone, crafts, face painting, ending in FIREWORKS), plus Finglas Fright Night, Edenmore Fireworks Display, Booh! Cabra & Glasnevin, Darndale Together After Dark, Crumlin and Brickfield Park festivals, and the Cabbage Patch Cauldron in D8.
options.source: https://www.bramstokerfestival.com/ + https://www.dublincity.ie/news/dublin-city-councils-seriously-scary-programme-halloween-events + https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/articles/cjr4y1j91x7o
options.experience_score: 5/10 — genuinely warm, free, authentic community Halloween, and Otherworld in Ballymun is a real event with real fireworks. But it is decentralised, suburban, and has no single headline spectacle. It is a perfectly good place to BE; it is not a reason to be there.
options.dates: DCC programme ~Oct 20–31 2026; Otherworld Oct 31, ~6–9pm, Ballymun
options.notes: 2026 neighbourhood listings publish on dublincity.ie closer to the date. ONE REAL ADVANTAGE OVER THE CONTINENT: Nov 1 2026 is a SUNDAY and is NOT an Irish public holiday (Ireland's October bank holiday was Oct 26). Normal Sunday trading, museums and pubs open — whereas Nov 1 is a solemn public holiday in both Austria and Italy. Your Nov 1 is more usable in Ireland than anywhere else on this list.

options.label: Dublin-area family attractions to fill Oct 27–29 (the gap before Derry)
options.detail: EMERALD PARK (Ashbourne, Co. Meath, ~20–35 min from Dublin) — Ireland's only theme park + zoo, runs a Halloween 'Tricky Trail' (Mad Professor Oswald's Wizards Potion Room, a Freaky Forest of witches and characters) INCLUDED with standard entry, historically on Oct 26–31; up to 20% early-bird discount if booked before midnight the night before. The single best all-three-ages option in the Dublin orbit. DUBLIN ZOO Halloween — special evening hours, pumpkin trails, costume parades; family ticket ~€65. THE HAUNTED TRAIL at Malahide Castle & Gardens — interactive outdoor Halloween experience with the castle's resident ghost Puck, a pumpkin patch and scarecrow (2026 dates TBC; also runs at Palmerstown House, Kildare). GHOST TOURS — note the age split: the Gravedigger Bus is adult-toned horror and often 18+, while 'Ghostbus Kids' is purpose-built for children. Plus EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, Trinity/Book of Kells, Guinness Storehouse and Dublinia for the standard rotation.
options.source: https://www.emeraldpark.ie/ + https://dublingazette.com/whats-on/events/emeraldpark-halloween-trickytrail-55533/ + https://www.dublinzoo.ie/ + https://www.thehauntedtrail.ie/malahide
options.experience_score: 7/10 as connective tissue — Emerald Park in particular genuinely works for 8, 13 and 16 simultaneously, and it sits in Co. Meath so it pairs naturally with a Púca day.
options.dates: Emerald Park Halloween typically Oct 26–31; verify 2026 on emeraldpark.ie
options.notes: Oct 31 2026 is a Saturday — book Emerald Park and Dublin Zoo well ahead. If you take the Oct 25 flight, these fill Oct 27–28 nicely, which are also the two days DBV–DUB was unbookable anyway.

options.label: RANK 6 — VIENNA PRATER HALLOWEEN, Oct 29–31. Your instinct was right: minor park dressing.
options.detail: Giving this the honest scoring you asked for. WHAT IS REAL: the Prater runs a genuine children's Halloween programme Oct 29–31 with FREE admission (pay per ride) — pumpkin carving, an interactive circus, craft stations for 'little witches, ghosts and vampires', children's theatre, walking acts and the Prater Wurstel handing sweets to costumed kids, free Dracula ice cream while stocks last, the Liliputbahn Ghost Train on Oct 31, and the Luftburg bouncy castles reskinned as a land of witches and magicians. A Halloween Parade of floats winds through the whole Prater at ~7pm on Oct 31. Bonus: the VIENNA HALLOWEEN RUN on Oct 30 in the decorated Prater has a Mini Monster Run (600/800m), Little Fear Run (2.5km) and Big Scare Run (5km) — all three of your kids could actually run something, which is a genuinely charming family memory. The Prater Dome's 10pm party is adults-only and irrelevant. NOV 1 PROBLEM: Nov 1 is Allerheiligen, an Austrian public holiday, AND the exact date the Prater flips to WINTER SEASON — attractions run daily only 15 Mar–31 Oct; from Nov 1 opening is limited, weather-dependent, decided individually by each operator at short notice, roughly noon–10pm. Year-round and safe: the Riesenrad, Madame Tussauds, Kingdom of Railroads, Kolarik bouncy castle, the rollercoaster restaurant. Austrian shops are closed Sundays AND holidays, so Nov 1 2026 is a double closure for retail; restaurants and major museums generally open.
options.source: https://www.praterwien.com/en/events/details/kids-halloween + https://prater.at/en/the-halloween-weekend/ + https://www.vienna-halloween-run.at/ + https://www.praterwien.com/en/faqs
options.experience_score: 4/10 AS A HALLOWEEN EXPERIENCE — you called it correctly. It is a fairground dressed for the season, not a cultural spectacle. It would delight the 8-year-old, mildly amuse the 13-year-old, and bore the 16-year-old. Austria has no deep Halloween tradition and it shows; the solemnity of Allerheiligen is the actual local observance and it is the opposite in mood.
options.dates: Oct 29–31 2026; parade ~7pm Oct 31; Halloween Run Oct 30
options.notes: Detailed timings above are from the 2025 edition; praterwien.com publishes exact 2026 timings closer to the date. Routing note: DBV–VIE at $199 (Oct 30) or $295 (Oct 25) is your cheapest exit from Dubrovnik, but you then still need FIVE seats VIE–DUB before Nov 2, which is unverified and re-opens the exact problem that has constrained this whole trip.

options.label: Vienna judged as a CITY rather than as Halloween — where it genuinely shines
options.detail: Separating the two, as you asked. Vienna is legitimately excellent for 16/13/8 in late October, just not because of Halloween. SCHÖNBRUNN — palace plus the Kindermuseum where kids dress in Baroque clothing and learn fan language, plus the Tiergarten (the world's OLDEST zoo), the maze, the Palm House and Desert House. HAUS DES MEERES — an Aqua Terra zoo with 10,000+ animals built inside a WWII anti-aircraft flak tower, with sharks, a rainforest section, a rooftop observation deck and a wartime museum in the structure itself; the building alone lands with teenagers (go midweek, one lift only). TECHNISCHES MUSEUM — right next to Schönbrunn, hands-on: high-voltage and steam-locomotive demonstrations, a hamster wheel you generate electricity in, 'Birdly' VR flight, minTi/miniXplore zones. NATURHISTORISCHES — the world's largest meteorite collection with a meteor-strike simulator, dinosaurs, free for kids. HAUS DER MUSIK — virtually conduct the Vienna Philharmonic, the waltz-dice game, musical stairs. Plus the Riesenrad, the Spanish Riding School's Morgenarbeit (far easier to get into than performances, and you can leave early), the Remise transport museum, and Naschmarkt with its Saturday flea market. Christmas markets do NOT open until mid-November, so that draw is unavailable.
options.source: https://www.wien.info/en/see-do/families/the-best-museums-for-children-413202 + https://www.altstadt.at/en/concierge/vienna-with-children/
options.experience_score: 7/10 as a city break for these three ages — strong, well-priced, easy, and the 16-year-old is well served by Haus des Meeres and the Technisches Museum. But this is a case FOR Vienna generally, not for Vienna ON HALLOWEEN. Going there Oct 30–Nov 1 means paying the Halloween opportunity cost for a city experience you could have any week of the year.
options.dates: Any time in the window; Nov 1 museums generally open, shops closed
options.notes: Vienna City Card gives family discounts on museums, attractions and transit. Lodging ~$91–180/night is the cheapest of your three candidate cities. Genuine verdict: Vienna is the right answer if the trip's priority quietly shifts from 'best Halloween' to 'best value city with happy kids' — but on the question you actually asked, it loses.

options.label: RULED OUT — Galway Macnas Parade (the real one) falls OUTSIDE your window
options.detail: Worth stating explicitly because it is the event the 2024 Dublin hoax impersonated. The genuine Macnas Halloween Parade is Ireland's largest free Halloween spectacle, drawing up to 80,000 people along a route from University of Galway via the Cathedral, Salmon Weir Bridge, Eglinton St, Shop St, Mainguard St and O'Brien's Bridge to the Claddagh — but Macnas parades on the OCTOBER BANK HOLIDAY weekend, and for 2026 that means expected Sunday Oct 25 at 5:30pm, not yet officially confirmed and the theme not yet announced. That is five days before your window opens.
options.source: https://www.galwaytourism.ie/event/macnas-halloween-parade/
options.experience_score: n/a for Oct 30–Nov 1 — it does not occur in your window. Even on the Oct 25 flight you would land the same day it runs, 2.5 hours away, and could not realistically make it.
options.dates: Expected Sun Oct 25 2026, 5:30pm, Galway (unconfirmed)
options.notes: Flagging it mainly as a fact-check anchor: if you see ANY listing claiming a Macnas parade in Dublin on Oct 31, that listing is fabricated. That exact claim is what put thousands on O'Connell Street in 2024.

leg: LANE B — Croatia ground/sea from Dubrovnik (ferry, charter, bus, rail) + the strategic Split-vs-Zagreb relocation question, Oct 25–Nov 1 2026
summary: The headline is not the ferry. It is Zagreb. I hit Ryanair's own timetable API and then drove ryanair.com with an actual 5-passenger party, and the capacity wall that makes Dubrovnik miserable does not exist at Zagreb: ZAG-DUB Oct 30 priced at $466.80 TOTAL for 5, confirmed on the fare-selection page. That is $1,183 under your verified DBV-DUB Oct 30 fare of $1,650. Zagreb is a Ryanair BASE with a based A320 fleet going 5-to-6 weekly on Dublin for winter 2026/27 (double on Saturdays); Dubrovnik's Dublin route is 2x weekly, which is exactly why Oct 27 and Oct 28 had 3 and 2 seats left. Zagreb also flies Oct 26, 29 and 31 — three dates Dubrovnik simply cannot do. Only Oct 28 is dark from ZAG. SPLIT IS A TRAP and I want to be blunt about it: Ryanair has ZERO departures from SPU to DUB, STN, VIE or BGY in the entire Oct 24–Nov 3 window (empty timetable response, not a fare issue), and Aer Lingus DUB-SPU has no availability from Oct 2026 through Apr 2027. Split shuts its Northern European network the day the IATA winter season starts, Oct 25. It is also the most expensive of the three cities for lodging. Relocating to Split as a BASE makes your flight problem worse and your lodging bill higher. On the ferry: the Oct 18 scare in prior research was real but it was the WRONG BOAT. TP Line route 654 does end 18.10.2026. But Kapetan Luka's Krilo Star (route 998) and TP Line route 842 both run daily through 31.10.2026, confirmed by two independent sources. The catamaran is alive. The nuance that matters more than the date: EU clocks fall back on Oct 25 2026, so Split sunset drops to about 16:46. The famous 15:30 Krilo sailing goes dark somewhere around Korcula and you pay 250 euro to look at black water past Hvar and Brac. Take the 08:00 TP Line 842 instead (arrives 13:25, full daylight the whole way) — but note 842 has NO Dubrovnik departure on Oct 31, so Oct 30 is your last daylight boat. Private charter is an off-season non-starter: fleets are hauled out, nobody publishes an October rate, bora season runs Oct-Apr, and a 5-6 hour open-water transfer is the single leg most likely to be scrubbed by weather. You would pay roughly 6-12x the public catamaran for the same water with a real chance of cancellation. Skip it. The best answer combines all of this: the STELLAR route (daylight catamaran through Mljet/Korcula/Hvar/Brac, a night in Split, 50-minute hop to Zagreb, Mirogoj on All Saints, then ZAG-DUB) costs about $1,050 in transport for 5 — which is $108 LESS than simply flying DBV-DUB direct on Nov 1. The memorable version is cheaper than the convenient version. That almost never happens, and it is the whole answer to this lane.
caveats: HARD-VERIFIED vs INFERRED — please read this before spending. (1) The $466.80 ZAG-DUB figure is the strongest number in this brief: I drove ryanair.com to the fare-selection page with a real 5-person party and read the party total off the page. Reaching that page IS the capacity proof — Ryanair blocks the search when it lacks seats. But I ran the first pass with mix ADT2/TEEN1/CHD2; the correct Ryanair banding for kids 16/13/8 is ADT3 (16 counts as an adult)/TEEN1/CHD1. I re-ran with the correct mix and the per-person fares were identical, so the total holds, but you should confirm at booking. (2) BAGS ARE NOT IN ANY OF THESE NUMBERS and this is the biggest single risk to the math. Ryanair Basic is one underseat bag only. A family of five ending a long trip needs checked luggage: Plus (20kg checked) is +$50.71/pp = +$253.55, Regular (10kg) is +$36.89/pp = +$184.45. Apply that to BOTH the Zagreb routing and your existing DBV-DUB quotes before comparing, and check whether your verified $813/$1,650/$1,158 DBV-DUB figures already include bags — if they do, my Zagreb numbers are understated relative to them. (3) Croatia Airlines fares (DBV-ZAG $362, SPU-ZAG $272) came from Google Flights priced as 5 ADULTS. Child fares may be slightly lower; treat these as ceilings, but they are live quotes for the actual dates. (4) The catamaran fare of 50 euro/pp is from two published operator fare tables, NOT a live booking. I could not get a late-Oct-2026 booking engine to return a quote — Krilo's own booking subdomain was unreachable and Ferryhopper redirected to home. Two independent sources agree on both the 50 euro fare and the 01.04-31.10.2026 season, which is why I rate the season date high confidence and the fare medium. CHILD DISCOUNT: do not budget for one. Multiple sources indicate discounts stop at infants (0-2, some say free to age 3). Kids 8, 13 and 16 all pay full adult fare. Verify with the operator before you build a plan around it. (5) Dubrovnik has NO railway station. Any Rome2Rio-style train result from Dubrovnik is a bus leg in disguise. Split-Zagreb rail does exist (roughly 6h) if you want a slower, cheaper alternative to the 50-minute SPU-ZAG flight. (6) Nov 1 2026 is a Sunday AND a Croatian national holiday (All Saints). Shops, markets and offices close. Buy food on Oct 31. It falls on a weekend so Croatian holidays do not roll to Monday — Nov 2 is a normal working day. (7) ZAG-DUB on Oct 26 spikes to $189.22/pp ($946 for 5) — a clear outlier against $93-115 on every other date. Avoid Oct 26 specifically. (8) November is the rainiest month on the Croatian coast and daylight is short (Split sunset about 16:46 after the clock change). Front-load outdoor sightseeing before 16:30. (9) I could not obtain a single published private-charter rate for October; my 1,500-3,000 euro range is inferred from summer rates, published one-way repositioning fees (300-1,000 euro) and operator quote-only pricing. Treat it as an order-of-magnitude sanity check, not a quote. (10) Schedules this far out are not final — the EX-YU report itself notes Croatian network changes remain possible. Re-verify the ZAG-DUB operating days before committing to non-refundable lodging.

options.label: THE CAPACITY BREAKER — Ryanair ZAG-DUB, 5 seats confirmed available
options.detail: Verified live on ryanair.com with a real 5-passenger party: ZAG-DUB Fri Oct 30 2026, FR2191 16:45-18:50, 3h05m, Basic fare, party total $466.80 (page-confirmed, not extrapolated). Per-person fares across the window for a 5-pax search: Oct 25 $102.21, Oct 26 $189.22, Oct 27 $99.68, Oct 29 $103.47, Oct 30 $93.36, Oct 31 $115.54, Nov 1 $101.26. Party-of-5 totals: Oct 25 $511, Oct 26 $946, Oct 27 $498, Oct 29 $517, Oct 30 $467, Oct 31 $578, Nov 1 $506. Operating days ZAG-DUB from Ryanair's own timetable API: Oct 25, 26, 27, 29, 30, 31 (TWO flights: FR8911 06:25 and FR2191 17:10), Nov 1, 2, 3. Only Oct 28 is dark. Compare Dubrovnik: DBV-DUB runs Oct 24, 25, 27, 28, 30, Nov 1, 3 — dark on Oct 26, 29 and 31. WHY the capacity differs: Zagreb is a Ryanair base with a based A320 fleet; Dublin goes from 5 to 6 weekly for winter 2026/27 with double Saturdays, alongside 13 weekly to Stansted with double-dailies. Dubrovnik's Dublin service is 2x weekly year-round in W26/27 — which is precisely why your Oct 27 and Oct 28 searches returned 3 and 2 seats. Zagreb carries roughly six times the weekly seats on the same city pair.
options.source: ryanair.com live 5-passenger booking flow, fare-selection page; services-api.ryanair.com/timtbl/3/schedules/ZAG/DUB/years/2026; exyuaviation.com Ryanair winter 2026/27 Zagreb report
options.experience_score: 7/10 — it is a Ryanair flight, so the experience is the CITY it unlocks, not the seat. But it converts a $1,650 problem into a $467 one and opens three dates Dubrovnik cannot fly at all.
options.notes: This single finding is worth more than everything else in this lane. Against your verified DBV-DUB Oct 30 fare of $1,650, the Zagreb leg alone is $1,183 cheaper before you add the connector.

options.label: THE CONNECTOR — Croatia Airlines DBV-ZAG, 55 minutes nonstop
options.detail: Croatia Airlines flies Dubrovnik-Zagreb nonstop in 55 minutes, roughly 3x daily, year-round (the airline runs about 20 weekly rotations through winter). Live Google Flights quote for 5: $362 total on the 06:40-07:35 departure; $435 total on the 16:20-17:15 or 17:20-18:15 departures. The only alternatives Google surfaced were absurd — SWISS/Lufthansa 2-stop via Zurich and Munich, 6h20m, $1,563. Verified separately that Ryanair does NOT fly DBV-ZAG or DBV-SPU at all (empty timetable response for both), so Croatia Airlines is the only sane air link north. FULL ROUTING MATH, Dubrovnik to Dublin via Zagreb: $362 + $467 (Oct 30) = $829 total for 5. Versus your verified DBV-DUB direct: Oct 30 $1,650 (SAVES $821), Nov 1 $1,158 (via ZAG on Nov 1: $362 + $506 = $868, SAVES $290), Oct 25 $813 (via ZAG: $362 + $511 = $873, costs $60 more — on Oct 25 the direct wins, take it). So the Zagreb routing is decisively better on every date EXCEPT Oct 25, and it is the ONLY option at all on Oct 26, 29 and 31.
options.source: Google Flights live query DBV-ZAG 2026-10-29, 5 passengers; services-api.ryanair.com timetable (DBV-ZAG and DBV-SPU both empty)
options.experience_score: 6/10 — 55 minutes, painless, and it buys back a whole day versus the 9.5-hour bus. With an 8-year-old that trade is not close.
options.notes: Take the 06:40 for the $73 saving only if the family tolerates a 5am start; otherwise the 16:20 at $435 lands you in Zagreb for dinner and is the better call with kids.

options.label: THE FERRY — ALIVE. Oct 18 scare was the wrong boat (correction to prior research)
options.detail: CORRECTION TO PRIOR RESEARCH: the Oct 18 date is real but it belongs to TP Line route 654 (first sailing 08.05.2026, LAST SAILING 18.10.2026). It is not the main coastal catamaran and it does not kill this option. Two lines run daily through 31.10.2026: (A) Kapetan Luka / Krilo Star, route 998 — Dubrovnik Gruz 15:30, Pomena/Mljet 16:50, Korcula Old Town 17:30, Hvar Town 18:50, Milna/Brac 19:30, Split 20:00. 4h30m, the fastest. (B) TP Line route 842 — Dubrovnik 08:00, arrives Split 13:25, 5h25m, via Korcula, Hvar, Milna. Season 01.04-31.10.2026 for both, confirmed by two independent sources. Fare 50 euro per person one-way, high and low season identical. FOR 5 = 250 euro, about $272. No child discount — treat all three kids as full fare (discounts appear to stop at infants 0-2). THE TIMING TRAP NOBODY MENTIONS: EU clocks fall back on Oct 25 2026 and Split sunset drops to roughly 16:46. The celebrated 15:30 Krilo sailing therefore loses daylight around Korcula and you spend the Hvar and Brac legs — the best part — staring at black water. TAKE THE 08:00 TP LINE 842 INSTEAD: it departs after sunrise (about 07:00 CET) and arrives 13:25, entirely in daylight. CRITICAL: route 842 has NO Dubrovnik departure on 31.10.2026, so Oct 30 is your last daylight boat of the season. Foot passengers only, no cars. 23kg luggage allowance per passenger on Krilo. Board 30 minutes early at Gruz.
options.source: absolute-dubrovnik.com Krilo 2026 timetable (valid 1.4.2026-31.10.2026); croatiaferries.com route pages 998 / 842 / 654 with first and last sailing dates; ferryhopper.com discount policy
options.dates: Daily 01.04-31.10.2026. Take route 842 (08:00) on or before Oct 30.
options.experience_score: 9/10 for the 08:00 daylight sailing — threading Mljet, Korcula, Hvar and Brac in one 5-hour run is one of the genuinely great European boat journeys, and a 16, 13 and 8-year-old will all be on deck for it. Drops to 4/10 for the 15:30 sailing after the clock change, where you pay the same money to sit in the dark.
options.notes: This is the single most stellar thing available in this lane, and it costs 250 euro. But the season end and the daylight window make Oct 30 a hard wall. Fare is from published tables, not a live booking — Krilo's booking subdomain was unreachable and Ferryhopper would not return a late-Oct 2026 quote, so confirm before building the trip around it.

options.label: SPLIT AS A BASE — UNAVAILABLE. Ryanair has zero SPU departures in the window
options.detail: This is the clearest negative finding in the lane and it kills the Split relocation idea outright. I queried Ryanair's timetable API for SPU to DUB, STN, VIE and BGY across Oct 24 - Nov 3 2026. ALL FOUR returned empty. Not expensive, not sold out — no service at all. Separately, Aer Lingus's own booking calendar shows no DUB-SPU availability from October 2026 through April 2027; the route is summer-seasonal. Croatia Airlines' SPU-DUB is likewise seasonal. Split Airport effectively shuts its Northern European network the day the IATA winter season begins on Oct 25 2026. On top of that, Split is the MOST expensive of your three candidate cities for a party of 5: central 2-bedroom units sleeping 4-5 run roughly $110-230/night in late October (Dubrovnik $78-120, Zagreb $100-165), because a family of 5 forces you into a 2-bedroom-plus-sofa at the top of the band. So relocating to Split as a BASE would simultaneously raise your lodging bill AND leave you with no way home except backtracking to Zagreb. It fails on both axes.
options.source: services-api.ryanair.com/timtbl/3/schedules/SPU/{DUB,STN,VIE,BGY}/years/2026/months/{10,11} — all empty; Aer Lingus booking calendar; Expedia/Booking.com October Split rate samples
options.dates: Oct 24 - Nov 3 2026
options.experience_score: 7/10 as a PLACE (Diocletian's Palace is a living neighbourhood, free to wander, highs about 19C/66F, sea still about 20C) — but 1/10 as a BASE, because you cannot fly out of it.
options.notes: Use Split as a half-day stopover at the end of the catamaran ride, then move on the same or next day. Do not book multiple nights here. The ticketed Palace elements (Cathedral of St Domnius, bell tower, substructures) go to reduced winter hours from November and may close on Nov 1.

options.label: ZAGREB AS A BASE — the sleeper, and All Saints at Mirogoj is the real prize
options.detail: Lodging: central 2-bedroom sleeping 5 runs roughly $100-165/night in late October (aggregator average about $112/night; listing range 70-250 euro). That is ABOVE Dubrovnik's $78-120, so Zagreb is not a lodging saving — the entire saving is in the airfare, and it is large enough that the lodging delta of $20-45/night is noise. What Zagreb actually offers a 16/13/8 spread on short, cool, possibly wet days: MIROGOJ CEMETERY on the evening of Oct 31 or on Nov 1 for All Saints (Svi sveti) — thousands of candles across a 19th-century monumental cemetery, free shuttle buses running from near the Cathedral, an atmosphere of genuine reverence, and essentially no tourists. Croatia has no real Halloween tradition; this is the actual observance and it is far more affecting than a themed event. Then: Museum of Illusions (best for roughly 7+, so all three kids), Technical Museum Nikola Tesla with a planetarium and a live Tesla coil demonstration (check demo times, they run only at set hours), Ethnographic Museum, Museum of Broken Relationships, Zagreb City Museum, and the Lotrscak Tower cannon fired daily at noon. Compact and walkable with trams, which matters when it is dark by 17:00. Advent has NOT started — that is late November, so you are not getting Zagreb's famous Christmas market.
options.source: Airbnb/likibu/cozycozy Zagreb rate aggregation; total-croatia-news and lovezagreb.hr on Mirogoj All Saints; timeanddate.com Croatia All Saints 2026; Zagreb family-attraction guides
options.dates: Oct 29 - Nov 1 2026, 2-3 nights
options.experience_score: 8/10 — Mirogoj on All Saints is a legitimately memorable, non-touristic thing that almost nobody plans for, and the indoor museum density is exactly right for short cold days with a wide kid age spread. Not a beach town, and Advent has not started, so it earns its score on atmosphere and museums rather than scenery.
options.notes: Nov 1 2026 is a Sunday AND a national holiday — shops, markets and offices closed. Buy food on Oct 31. Croatian holidays do not roll to Monday, so Nov 2 is a normal working day. Price shown is per-night midpoint, not a party total.

options.label: BUS Dubrovnik-Split — cheapest link, genuinely fine with an 8-year-old
options.detail: FlixBus live 'from' fare of 19.98 euro per person on the Dubrovnik-Split route, so roughly 100 euro / about $110 for 5 booked ahead. Journey 3h55m-4h15m, about 12 departures a day from 03:30 to 21:05. Since the Peljesac Bridge opened the route stays entirely inside Croatia — no Neum corridor, no two Bosnian border checks, which used to be the single worst part of this ride and is the reason older advice about this leg is stale. One 7kg carry-on plus one 20kg checked bag included per passenger, mobile ticket. Stations are Obala pape Ivana Pavla II 44 in Dubrovnik and Obala kneza Domagoja 12 in Split, both central. Arriva, Nomago and Promet Makarska also run it; Arriva rates best on cleanliness, Nomago on punctuality. Four hours with no border stops is entirely manageable for an 8-year-old.
options.source: global.flixbus.com/bus-routes/bus-dubrovnik-split live 'from 19,98 EUR'; Omio, Wanderu, Rome2Rio cross-checks
options.dates: Daily, ~12 departures, 03:30-21:05
options.experience_score: 5/10 — competent, cheap, comfortable enough, scenically decent along the Makarska Riviera. It is transport, not an experience. If the boat is running and the weather holds, pay the extra ~$160 for the catamaran instead; if the sea is rough or you are travelling after Oct 30, this is the right fallback.

options.label: BUS Dubrovnik-Zagreb — do NOT do this, it is a false economy
options.detail: FlixBus, Nomago, Arriva and Samoborcek all run it, roughly 6-10 departures a day, 625 km. Journey 9h30m to 11h; the fastest quoted is 8h10m (Nomago). Fares roughly 28-55 dollars per person, so about $170-275 for 5. Overnight service departs Dubrovnik 22:00 and arrives Zagreb 07:00, and yes it saves a hotel night. But compare honestly against the 55-minute Croatia Airlines flight at $362 for 5: you save at most about $190, and you pay for it with a 9-to-11 hour overnight coach with an 8-year-old, arriving wrecked at 07:00 with a full day to fill before check-in. Against a trip framed around not squandering stellar experiences, this is the worst dollar-per-misery trade available in the lane.
options.source: FlixBus, Busbud, Virail, Rome2Rio route listings for Dubrovnik-Zagreb
options.dates: Daily, earliest 03:30, overnight departs 22:00 arriving 07:00
options.experience_score: 2/10 — the saving is real but small, and the cost in exhaustion with a young child is disproportionate. Included for completeness and honestly priced; my recommendation is to reject it.
options.notes: Also note: Dubrovnik has NO railway station at all. Any 'train from Dubrovnik' result is a bus leg in disguise. Split-Zagreb rail does exist (about 6h) as a slower cheaper alternative to the SPU-ZAG flight if you take the boat north first.

options.label: PRIVATE CHARTER Dubrovnik-Split — off-season non-starter, skip it
options.detail: Honest answer: this is the one option in the lane I would tell you to drop. Nobody publishes an October rate. The Marinero private transfer (5-6 hours, two professional crew, fuel and onboard drinks included, fully customisable departure time) is quote-only with no stated capacity, no stated season and no published weather policy. Inferring from adjacent data — one-way repositioning fees alone run 300-1,000 euro (about 1,000 for gulets), and a week's yacht charter drops from about 4,000 euro in summer to 2,500-3,000 in June/September — a bespoke 5-6 hour crewed transfer in late October realistically lands somewhere around 1,500-3,000 euro. That is roughly 6 to 12 times the public catamaran for substantially the same water. The bigger problem is not price, it is deliverability: bora and sirocco season runs October to April, bora reaches force 5-7 with gusts of 40-60 knots and builds fast, and a long open-water transfer is explicitly the leg most likely to be scrubbed. Many fleets are already lifted out by October. One genuine mitigation: the worst bora is concentrated around the Velebit range well NORTH of the Dubrovnik-Split corridor, so your route is not the worst-affected stretch — but that lowers the risk, it does not remove it.
options.source: dubrovnikboatstour.com Marinero private transfer page (quote-only, no price/capacity/season published); secret-adriatic and yacht-rent one-way repositioning fee ranges; sea-help.eu and simarine.net on bora; skippercity/splendidyachting October sailing conditions
options.dates: Late Oct 2026, availability unconfirmed
options.experience_score: 6/10 in the abstract, 3/10 as an actual plan for these dates. A private boat through the Dalmatian islands is a genuinely stellar thing in September. In the last week of October it is an expensive coin-flip with fleets laid up, and a scrub strands you needing a same-day replacement.
options.notes: Price is an order-of-magnitude inference, NOT a quote — no operator would publish one. If you want the boat experience, the 08:00 TP Line 842 catamaran delivers about 90 percent of the same route and the same island stops for 250 euro, on a vessel that runs regardless of whether a charter skipper decides to sail.

options.label: NET VERDICT A — THE STELLAR ROUTE. Cheaper than flying direct.
options.detail: Dubrovnik through Oct 29. Oct 30: TP Line route 842 catamaran, Dubrovnik Gruz 08:00 to Split 13:25, full daylight through Korcula, Hvar and Milna (Brac) — about $272 for 5. Afternoon and one night in Split, wandering Diocletian's Palace. Oct 31: Croatia Airlines SPU-ZAG nonstop, about 50 minutes, live-quoted at $272 for 5. Evening of Oct 31 or the day of Nov 1: Mirogoj for All Saints, thousands of candles, free shuttle from the Cathedral. Nov 1: Ryanair ZAG-DUB, $506 for 5. Into Dublin with time to spare before EI61. TRANSPORT TOTAL: about $1,050 for 5. Your verified DBV-DUB direct on Nov 1 is $1,158. THE STELLAR VERSION IS $108 CHEAPER THAN THE CONVENIENT VERSION, and it adds one of Europe's great boat journeys, a night in Diocletian's Palace, and All Saints at Mirogoj. That inversion is the answer to this lane. If you would rather be in Dublin for Halloween itself, swap to ZAG-DUB on Oct 31 ($578, and there are two flights that day) and compress Zagreb to a single night — total about $1,122, still under the direct fare.
options.source: Composite: TP Line 842 published fare table (50 EUR/pp); Google Flights live SPU-ZAG 2026-10-30 5 pax ($272); ryanair.com live 5-pax ZAG-DUB Nov 1 ($101.26/pp)
options.dates: Oct 30 boat, Oct 31 hop, Nov 1 fly to Dublin
options.experience_score: 9/10 — three genuinely distinct experiences (Dalmatian island catamaran in daylight, Diocletian's Palace, All Saints at Mirogoj) for less than the price of sitting on one Ryanair flight. This is the one to build around.
options.notes: Two hard dependencies: the catamaran fare is from published tables not a live booking, and route 842 has no Dubrovnik departure on Oct 31 so Oct 30 is the last daylight sailing. Confirm the boat first; if it will not confirm, fall back to Verdict B.

options.label: NET VERDICT B — THE EFFICIENT ROUTE. Maximum saving, minimum friction.
options.detail: Skip the boat entirely. Dubrovnik through Oct 29 or 30. Croatia Airlines DBV-ZAG nonstop, 55 minutes, $362 for 5 (take the 16:20 for a civilised departure). Two nights in Zagreb at roughly $100-165/night, covering Mirogoj for All Saints plus the Museum of Illusions and the Technical Museum Nikola Tesla for the kids. Then Ryanair ZAG-DUB: Oct 30 $467, Oct 31 $578 (two flights, gets you to Dublin ON Halloween), or Nov 1 $506. TRANSPORT TOTAL: $829 (Oct 30) to $940 (Oct 31). Against your verified directs that is a saving of $821 on Oct 30 and $290 on Nov 1, and it makes Oct 26, 29 and 31 possible at all — three dates on which Dubrovnik simply has no flight. One honest exception: on Oct 25 the direct DBV-DUB at $813 beats routing via Zagreb ($873). If you want to leave Croatia on Oct 25, take the direct and skip this whole lane.
options.source: Google Flights live DBV-ZAG 5 pax ($362); ryanair.com live 5-pax ZAG-DUB fare page (Oct 30 total $466.80 confirmed)
options.dates: Fly north Oct 29 or 30; ZAG-DUB Oct 30, 31 or Nov 1
options.experience_score: 7/10 — you trade the catamaran (the single best thing on offer) for simplicity and the biggest dollar saving in the lane. Zagreb plus Mirogoj still carries it well above a plain transfer day.
options.notes: Add bags to this before comparing to any quote that includes them: Ryanair Plus (20kg checked) is +$253.55 for the party, Regular (10kg) +$184.45. Avoid Oct 26 — it spikes to $946 for 5, an outlier against $93-115/pp on every other date.
